episode.title: Reject runtime wrapper instances as provider error bodies
episode.before: At parent commit 66cd061ab468aeae9fd2e38715d3931f7f77f569, provider error normalization treated every non-null object with enumerable keys as a usable body. Node-style streams with a pipe method were excluded, but class instances and wrapper objects without pipe were JSON-serialized. Downstream formatting could then select serialized implementation internals instead of the diagnostic Error.message.
episode.after: At commit 4523528b21c66084fdece7ed3ffa10888bc5ac60, object-valued body candidates are accepted only when non-empty and their prototype is Object.prototype or null. Class instances and response wrappers are rejected, leaving body undefined so downstream formatting preserves Error.message; strings and plain parsed JSON objects remain supported.
episode.diff: The change replaced isNonEmptyObject with isPlainNonEmptyObject for both the nested error field and response-body field. The new predicate checks value type, null, prototype identity, and enumerable-key count. Three regression tests cover rejection of a response-body class instance, rejection of a nested-error class instance, and continued serialization of a plain parsed JSON object. No provider call sites or formatter branches were changed.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit is 4523528b21c66084fdece7ed3ffa10888bc5ac60, its parent is 66cd061ab468aeae9fd2e38715d3931f7f77f569, and it changes the shared error-body utility plus its unit test.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --stat 4523528b21c66084fdece7ed3ffa10888bc5ac60; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit, parent_commit, and changed_files_name_status

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation serialized any non-null, non-empty object found in error.error or error.$response.body, except response bodies recognized by the separate pipe-method stream check.
evidence_units.source: git show 66cd061ab468aeae9fd2e38715d3931f7f77f569:packages/ai/src/utils/error-body.ts, pickBodyText, isReadableStreamLike, and isNonEmptyObject

evidence_units.claim: The pinned change replaces both generic non-empty-object checks with a plain-object predicate that accepts only Object.prototype or null prototypes and still requires at least one enumerable key.
After the change, string bodies remain directly usable, pipe-like response streams remain excluded, class-instance object bodies are rejected, and non-empty plain objects remain JSON-serialized.
The normalized result controls displayed provider failures: the shared formatter uses Error.message whenever no accepted body exists, while otherwise it may format status and body.
The Bedrock error adapter explicitly chooses normalized status and body only when messageCarriesBody is false and both values exist; otherwise it uses the normalized message.

At the pinned ref, the shared normalizer or formatter is used by Bedrock, OpenAI-compatible, Azure OpenAI, Google, and image-provider error paths, so the classification boundary is shared across multiple adapters.
A regression test supplies a response-body class instance without a pipe method and asserts that no body is extracted, the useful 'Input is too long' message remains, and messageCarriesBody is true.
A regression test supplies a class instance in the nested error field and asserts that it is not serialized and that 'TLS handshake failed' remains the normalized message.
A compatibility test supplies a non-empty plain parsed JSON body and asserts that it is still serialized and marked as separate from the opaque SDK message.
The added assertions jointly define the validation oracle: reject non-plain runtime objects from both supported object-valued slots while continuing to surface legitimate plain structured payloads.

candidate_atomics.name: admit-only-plain-structured-error-bodies
candidate_atomics.title: Accept only plain structured objects as error bodies
candidate_atomics.description: Guard object-valued provider error fields by prototype and content before serialization. Preserve string bodies and non-empty plain parsed payloads, but treat class instances, response wrappers, streams, nulls, and empty objects as absent bodies so diagnostic messages are not displaced by serialized internals.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent runtime transport or SDK wrapper state from replacing a useful provider diagnostic while retaining legitimate structured error payloads.
semantic_action.module_role: Shared provider-error payload classifier and normalizer
semantic_action.pre_state: An error has an object-valued candidate in a supported body slot, and the existing normalizer would serialize any non-empty object unless it exposed a node-style pipe method.
semantic_action.post_state: Only non-empty objects with Object.prototype or null prototype are serialized as structured bodies; rejected runtime objects yield no body, causing downstream formatting to retain the diagnostic message.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise both object-valued body slots with class instances and assert body is undefined and the original message survives; exercise a non-empty plain object and assert its serialized payload still becomes the normalized body.
parameters: candidate body slot: nested error field or response body field

candidate_workflows.name: normalize-ambiguous-provider-error-object-payloads
candidate_workflows.title: Normalize ambiguous object-valued provider error payloads without losing diagnostics
candidate_workflows.description: Tighten a shared error-normalization boundary when SDK fields may contain either parsed payloads or runtime wrapper instances. Establish the accepted structured-body shape, apply it consistently to every object-valued candidate slot, and validate both rejection and compatibility behavior.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure displayed provider failures use genuine structured payloads when available and otherwise preserve the useful diagnostic message instead of serialized SDK or transport internals.
when_to_use: A provider or transport SDK stores heterogeneous values in fields treated as error bodies.
Displayed errors contain serialized wrapper internals or stream state instead of the exception message.
Existing filtering recognizes only a specific runtime capability, such as a pipe method, and misses other class-based wrappers.
anti_goals: Do not remove support for string error bodies.
Do not suppress non-empty plain parsed JSON payloads merely because they are object-valued.
Do not redesign provider-specific call sites or error-message prefixes when the defect is in the shared payload-admission boundary.
Do not infer body legitimacy from serializability or enumerable keys alone.
not_applicable_when: The candidate payload is already governed by a reliable typed or schema-validated body contract.
The error corruption occurs after normalization and is unrelated to selecting an object-valued body.
The runtime value must intentionally support custom-prototype records as documented payloads; this exact plain-object rule would require a different compatibility contract.
inputs: Representative failing error containing a runtime wrapper or class instance
The object-valued fields probed as possible bodies
The fallback diagnostic message that must survive rejection
Representative legitimate string and plain structured bodies
Downstream formatter behavior when normalized body is absent or present
workflow_graph.entry_state: The normalizer accepts non-empty arbitrary objects as bodies, allowing serializable wrapper state to supersede the diagnostic message.
workflow_graph.exit_state: All supported object-valued body slots share a plain-object admission rule; wrapper instances are absent bodies, diagnostic messages survive, and legitimate plain structured payloads remain visible.

steps.condition: Apply when a body slot can contain either parsed structured data or SDK/transport runtime objects.
steps.validation: Regression assertions reject class instances in each supported object-valued slot and retain their messages, while a plain parsed object remains serializable as the body.

validation_ladder: Unit-check a class-instance response body without a node-style pipe method: body must be absent and the diagnostic message must survive.
Unit-check a class instance in the alternate nested error slot: body must be absent and the diagnostic message must remain exact.
Compatibility-check a non-empty plain parsed object: it must still serialize into the normalized body.
Confirm downstream formatting selects the message when no body is admitted and selects status/body only for an admitted separate body.
Inspect all shared-normalizer call sites to verify the central guard covers affected adapters without provider-specific duplication.
stop_conditions: Stop if the failing value is a documented custom-prototype payload that must be surfaced; define a different admissibility contract before changing behavior.
Stop if no downstream path prefers the normalized body over the message, because the observed symptom then has another cause.
Stop if representative legitimate structured payloads cannot be distinguished from runtime wrappers with an evidence-backed invariant.
